t: Minimum Flips in Binary Tree to Get Result
o: Leaves hold booleans; internal nodes apply OR(2)/AND(3)/XOR(4)/NOT(5). Flipping a leaf costs 1; find the minimum flips so the root evaluates to the given result. Tree DP: for each node compute the pair (min flips to evaluate false, min flips to evaluate true) bottom-up. Example 1's AND/OR/XOR mix needs 2 flips; example 2's leaf already matches, costing 0.
k: Each node needs only two numbers: cost of being false and cost of being true.
Combine children costs per operator: OR-false = both false, OR-true = min of the three other combos; dual for AND; XOR mixes both.
NOT simply swaps the child's pair.

a.i: DFS returns [costFalse, costTrue]. Leaves return [val, 1-val]. Internal nodes combine children per their operator's truth table, taking minima over the combinations that produce each output. Answer is the requested component at the root.
s: OR: false=lF+rF; true=min(lT+rT,lT+rF,lF+rT). AND: mirror. XOR: false=min(lT+rF,lF+rT); true=min(lT+rT,lF+rF).
a.t: O(N) — each node visited once with O(1) combination work.
a.sp: O(H) recursion stack, H = tree height (worst O(N)).

w: The truth tables are the entire difficulty — derive them from the definition (to make OR false, both children must be false, etc.) rather than memorizing. Pitfalls: NOT nodes may hang their single child on either side (handle null), and leaves must be detected before checking children. Follow-up: return the actual set of leaves to flip (track argmin choices), or generalize to n-ary gates.
